reasons: Cited text supports the compliant classification: 19.1 gives the professional/workmanlike standard plus material conformity to documentation; 19.2 gives a 90-day Deliverable warranty measured from the later of delivery or acceptance and a term-long hosted-Services conformance warranty; 19.4 supplies re-performance/repair/replacement with a termination-and-refund backstop; 19.3 adds compliance with Applicable Law and no malicious code.

No walk-away trigger: there is no 'AS IS' language, and 19.5 limits the disclaimer to implied warranties and expressly states that no disclaimer cuts down an express warranty or stated remedy, so the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranties.

The failed deterministic period check is a phrasing artifact — the document writes 'ninety days' rather than '90' or 'ninety (90)' — and the rationale correctly identifies this rather than treating it as a shortfall; the 90-day period meets the preferred services/deliverable threshold.
Correctly handled as a compliant finding: no redline and no counterparty comment proposed, consistent with retaining it as internal evaluation evidence rather than raising a negotiation issue.
